howto.name: Upload a signed PDF
howto.text: Drop a PDF with one or more digital signatures.

howto.name: PrivaTools verifies each signature
howto.text: Checks that the signed content hasn't been modified since signing, the certificate chain is intact, and the signing date is consistent.

howto.name: Read the report
howto.text: For each signature: signer name, signing time, certificate authority, validity status (valid / modified / expired / untrusted CA).

faq.q: Does this require uploading my certificates?
faq.a: No — verification uses the certificates embedded in the PDF itself, plus the system's trusted CA store.

faq.q: What if a signature is invalid?
faq.a: The report says exactly why: content modified, certificate expired, untrusted issuer, or signature format unsupported. The PDF itself isn't rejected — just the signature.
Yes — PDFs can have multiple signatures (e.g. one per signing party). All are verified independently.
